flags.note: The purpose clause 'so that there would not be' uses periphrastic construction typical of Greek influence. Native Hebrew would more likely use לְבִלְתִּי or simple לֹא with an infinitive construct.

While שֶׁ relatives are standard in Mishnaic Hebrew, the participial phrase 'הַנּוּתַן לָהֶם' (who were given to them) shows potential Greek passive influence rather than native Hebrew active construction.
The passive participle construction mirrors Greek syntax. Native Hebrew would more likely use an active construction or different verbal form.
The relative clause structure with modal verb 'that could not be counted' reflects Greek relative clause patterns. Native Hebrew would likely use אֲשֶׁר or a different construction.
The feminine pronoun 'והיא' appears without clear antecedent and seems to be a mechanical translation error from Greek, possibly reflecting a Greek conjunction or particle that was misunderstood.
